explanation: Requested a 5-step scan of cos(theta*) from -1 to +1 at W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.5 GeV^2, phi*=90 deg for the eta channel. A linear 5-step scan over [-1, +1] lands exactly on the endpoints cos(theta*) = -1.0 and +1.0, which are known integration poles for EXCLURAD's Fortran integrator (division by sin(theta*) type singularities in the exclusive kinematics); the eta channel documentation explicitly flags this and mandates using +/-0.999 instead of the exact poles. I therefore corrected the two endpoint values from -1.0/+1.0 to -0.999/+0.999 and kept the three interior points (-0.5, 0.0, 0.5) unchanged, producing the 5-point grid: -0.999, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 0.999. All 5 points passed preflight (threshold, Q2 positivity, beam-energy accessibility, lookup-table coverage, phi range, vcut sanity) with no warnings. One input file was generated (all 5 points fit within the 10-point-per-file chunking convention) at beam energy defaulting to the eta channel's 6.53 GeV and vcut=0.166 GeV^2.
